angle: Trust is now a KPI; treat AI content like regulated comms.
sourceTitle: Over 1 million people clicked LinkedIn’s ‘seems like AI slop’ button
linkedinPost:
Over 1 million people hit “seems like AI slop” on LinkedIn. That’s your customers and candidates voting with their thumbs.

Fortune covers the backlash. One analysis tagged 40% of long-form posts as fully AI-generated. As someone shipping AI into customer-facing workflows, here’s the blunt truth: if you don’t operationalize trust, AI will quietly torch your brand and funnel.

What we implement with clients:
- Label AI-assisted content; require sources for claims.
- Maintain a prompt and source library — reuse what’s verified.
- Add editorial QA and fact-check as a standard control, not a last-minute fix.
- Track “trust KPIs”: complaint rate, bounce/unsubscribe, time-on-page, and correction volume.
- Escalate risky topics to humans by policy, not vibe.

My take: treat AI content like regulated communications — discoverable, reviewable, attributable. The compliance burden is cheaper than rebuilding trust.

How are you measuring trust in your AI-assisted content today — and who signs off before it ships? #EnterpriseAI #AIAdoption #CustomerExperience
xPost: AI content without governance is brand debt. Label it, cite it, QA it, and track trust KPIs — or pay with churn and complaints later. Treat AI comms like regulated comms. #EnterpriseAI #CustomerExperience
